tasks.short: Write contact notes after visits, file documents in the case, prepare progress reports, get them signed, send them and register contacts for billing.

steps.what: Social worker types contact notes after each home visit from handwritten notes

loop.input: The visit recording, made only when the family consents, and the case file's contact note headings.
loop.output: A draft contact note under the headings, each sentence linked to its moment in the recording.
loop.check: A validator lists every statement about abuse, violence, self-harm, drugs or neglect that cannot be found in the transcript; the worker must resolve each one, then approves the note; nothing reaches the case file without approval.
loop.stop: One draft per visit; if consent is refused or the draft fails, the worker writes from notes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Home visits are free conversation; a form cannot turn them into a readable note.

steps.what: Social worker files letters, decisions and school documents in the case history records
Social worker prepares reports on progress for the municipality or court
Team leader reviews and signs the progress report
Social worker sends the signed report to the municipality or court by secure mail
Social worker tallies contacts and hours for the municipality's billing

tasks.design: With the family's consent a bounded step drafts the contact note from the visit recording in the youth care case system ({OTHER}), and a validator lists risk statements not found in the transcript; the worker resolves them and approves. Progress reports start from a template filled with case data (contacts, goals, status) for the worker to write the analysis; after the team leader signs, the report goes through the secure exchange, and contacts and hours flow from the notes to the municipality's registration.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed after visits, reports written from scratch, and contacts tallied in spreadsheets.
tasks.enabler_now: Dutch social teams pilot drafting reports from recorded talks with a worker checking every output, and municipalities and providers exchange youth care messages through national standards.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts have contained invented risk statements in reported cases; many families will not be recorded; a report about a child must be the worker's own judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Writing a report that is fair to the parents and honest about the child's safety.
tasks.altitude: The worker approves drafts and writes the analysis; the team leader still signs.

reach.learn: Whether prefilled reports make reviews faster.

evidence.claim: A Dutch social team records intakes and drafts the report with language models; a worker checks every output and a DPIA was done.
In a UK council pilot with 20 children's social care staff, practitioners self-reported about 11 hours a week saved, weekly admin down 46% and assessments submitted 65% faster.
UK social workers found invented suicidal ideation and irrelevant content in AI-drafted notes.
Municipalities and providers exchange youth care messages through national standards.
Recording staff conversations needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from visit notes to the report sent and contacts registered; decisions by the municipality or court are outside.
Input contract: recording consent asked and stored by the worker; note headings and report template set by the team leader; message standards from the municipality's system; fallback is typing.
Drafting runs under a processing agreement after a DPIA.
Team leader time is outside the worker's savings.
unknowns: Share of families who consent to recording.
research_questions: How often does the validator flag a statement that was not said?

already_counted.description: Social worker resolves validator flags and approves each note.
Social worker checks prefilled report data.

incremental.description: Social worker asks for recording consent and handles refusals.
Information manager audits samples of drafted notes.

approvals.approved_version: The contact note text as approved by the worker; later edits are new versions.
The progress report version signed by the team leader in s4; any change needs a new signature.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Families who refuse recording and complex cases leave more writing by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read the referral, interview the child and family, assess their situation and needs, and record the assessment.

steps.what: Social worker reads the referral and file before meeting the family
Social worker interviews clients individually, in families or in groups
Social worker assesses situations, capabilities and problems to determine services required
Social worker writes up the assessment in free text

tasks.design: The assessment is recorded in a structured form in the youth care case system ({OTHER}) with the team's agreed domains (safety, health, school, family, income) and the referral data filled in. The interview and the assessment itself stay fully with the worker; no AI scores the family.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assessments were written as free text, so each one was structured differently.
tasks.enabler_now: Case systems support structured assessment forms.
tasks.still_hard: Families' situations do not fit boxes; the free text remains essential.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what the family does not say and building enough trust to hear it.

reach.learn: Whether structured domains show where services fall short.

evidence.claim: Case systems support structured assessment forms with free-text fields.
AI that evaluates eligibility for public assistance is high-risk; this design uses no AI in the assessment.

assumptions: Boundary: from the referral to the recorded assessment; decisions on services are outside.
Input contract: assessment domains agreed by the team leader; referral data from the municipality's system; fallback is free text.
Interviews and assessment do not change.
No profiling or risk scoring is added.
research_questions: Do structured domains make handovers between workers easier?

incremental.description: Social worker learns the structured form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Almost all of this task is talking and judging.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Phone and message schools, doctors, courts and services, join multidisciplinary meetings, record consent to share, refer to providers and keep the child's network current.

steps.what: Social worker serves as liaison by phoning schools, doctors and services about the child
Social worker attends multidisciplinary meetings about children who face abuse, disabilities or poverty
Social worker asks parents for consent to share information and notes it on paper
Social worker e-mails referrals to youth care providers
Social worker keeps the child's contacts in a notebook

tasks.design: The case system ({OTHER}) keeps the child's network (school, GP, providers, court contacts) and the parents' consent per party with its scope and end date, so the worker knows who may be told what. Routine updates go as secure messages instead of phone tag, and referrals use the national youth care message standard; meetings and difficult calls stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Contacts and consents were in notebooks, and every update needed a phone call.
tasks.enabler_now: Municipalities and providers exchange youth care messages through national standards; case systems support secure messages.
tasks.still_hard: Schools and doctors use different systems; trust between parties is built by talking.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a school, a GP and a worried parent to agree on one plan for a child.

reach.learn: Whether shared consent records speed up joint work.

evidence.claim: Municipalities and providers exchange youth care messages through national standards.
Health data about a child is special-category data; sharing needs a legal basis such as consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from contacting partners to referrals made; the services themselves are outside.
Input contract: consents recorded by the worker with the parents; partner contacts added by the worker; message standards from the municipality's system; fallback is phone and e-mail.
Partners' time is outside the worker's savings.
unknowns: Which partners can receive secure messages.
research_questions: Do recorded consents prevent information being shared without a basis?

incremental.description: Social worker keeps consents and the network current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Partners who only phone keep most of the calls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Make the family plan with the family, write it down, check services were delivered, review progress together and keep review dates.

steps.what: Social worker develops the service plan in consultation with the family
Social worker writes the plan with goals, actions and dates as a document
Social worker checks with providers the quantity and quality of services provided
Social worker reviews progress with the family at follow-ups
Social worker sets reminders for plan reviews in a paper diary

tasks.design: The plan is written in a structured form in the youth care case system ({OTHER}) with goals, actions, who and when, and its review dates create tasks automatically. Start and stop messages from providers through the national standard show whether services began and how much was delivered, so the worker calls only where something is off; planning and reviewing with the family stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were documents, delivery was checked by phone, and review dates sat in diaries.
tasks.enabler_now: Municipalities and providers exchange youth care start and stop messages through national standards.
tasks.still_hard: Messages show quantity, not quality; quality comes from the family's own account.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a family set goals they believe in.

ambition.what: Every plan reviewed on time, with delivery gaps spotted before the review.

reach.learn: Whether delivery gaps show up per provider.

evidence.claim: Municipalities and providers exchange youth care messages through national standards.
Youth care staff spend about 38% of their time on administration, the most of client-facing jobs.
No decision with significant effect on a family may be based solely on automated processing; this design only shows data.

assumptions: Boundary: from making the plan to reviewing it; services delivered are outside.
Input contract: start and stop messages sent by providers; plan form set by the team leader; fallback is phone checks and diaries.
Provider time is outside the worker's savings.
Planning and reviewing with the family do not change.
research_questions: Do delivery gaps get noticed earlier with message data?

already_counted.description: Social worker reviews flagged delivery gaps.

incremental.description: Social worker learns the structured plan form.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Providers who send incomplete messages still need calls.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The family social worker keeps interviews, judgement and coordination; typing, tallies and phone checks shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A social worker who spends most of the week with families and partners, with records that are current without evenings at a keyboard.

job.title: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
